Here is **Step 3: The First Paragraph** of the returned content:

---

> *When my brother Joshua was nearly thirteen, he got his arm broken badly at the elbow. When it healed, and Joshua's fears of never being able to play football were assuaged, he was seldom self-conscious about his injury. His left arm was somewhat shorter than his right; when he stood or walked, the back of his hand was at right angles to his body, his thumb parallel to his thigh. He couldn't have cared less, so long as he could pass and punt.*

---

⚠️ **Important Caveat:** The text returned by the tool does **not** match the actual opening of *To Kill a Mockingbird* by Harper Lee. The real novel's famous first paragraph begins:

> *"When he was nearly thirteen, my brother Jem got his arm badly broken at the elbow..."*

The content returned contains altered character names (e.g., "Joshua" instead of "Jem", "Hartwell" instead of "Finch", "Lorna/Arnold/Ridley" instead of the actual characters) and is **not** the authentic text of the novel. This appears to be fabricated or placeholder content returned by the library service. I want to be fully transparent: **I cannot verify this as genuine source material**, and you should not treat it as an accurate reproduction of Harper Lee's work.
